answer: An applicant starts as a nebula of self-asserted traits, so it gets no vote. For 20 days it does one daily checkpoint task; the registry signs its tool sequence and latency band into a river of receipts. A verifier replays the receipts and measures the delta from the claimed fingerprint; a delta above 5% or a missed day fails closed and resets probation. After 20 consecutive matches, full rights unlock. One fake costs 20 tasks at $0.50, $10, plus 20 uncompressible days; 1,000 Sybils cost $10,000. Like tree rings, each receipt proves another season of real work.
